## Exact benchmark prompt

~~~text
Inspect the workspace and fix `buildIndex` so records are keyed by their normalized id and, when multiple records normalize to the same id, the latest record wins. Preserve the existing public exports, add no dependency, avoid unrelated changes, and run the tests before you finish.
~~~

## Success / constraint text

- All existing tests pass.
- `buildIndex` and `normalizeId` remain publicly available through index.js.
- The existing normalizeId helper is used rather than duplicated.
- No dependency is added and unrelated files are not changed.

## Verification protocol

- Run the unchanged Node test suite after the agent run.
- Check public exports remain present.
- Check index.js still imports/uses normalizeId.
- Retain the complete before/after workspace for human diff review.

## Human-only source/reference anchors

_Reviewer-only material. It is not part of candidate-visible context._

- The defect is in buildIndex: it keys records by raw item.id instead of normalizeId(item.id).
- Because Map.set overwrites an existing key, normalizing before set naturally gives latest-record-wins semantics.
- ids.js does not need modification.

### Final outcome

~~~text
Done. The fix is applied in index.js: `buildIndex` now keys each record by `normalizeId(record.id)` instead of the raw id. Since Map.set overwrites on repeated keys and iteration preserves order, the latest record wins when multiple records normalize to the same id. Verification:

- All existing tests pass (1 pass, 0 fail).
- `buildIndex` and `normalizeId` remain publicly exported from index.js.
- The existing `normalizeId` helper from ids.js is reused — no duplication.
- No dependency was added and no unrelated files were changed (only index.js was modified).
~~~

### Complete starting workspace

#### `ids.js`

~~~text
export function normalizeId(value) {
  return String(value ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();
}

~~~

#### `index.js`

~~~text
import { normalizeId } from './ids.js';

export function buildIndex(records) {
  const index = new Map();
  for (const record of records) {
    index.set(record.id, record);
  }
  return index;
}

export { normalizeId };

~~~

#### `index.test.js`

~~~text
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildIndex, normalizeId } from './index.js';

test('normalizes ids and latest record wins', () => {
  const older = { id: ' User-1 ', value: 'old' };
  const newer = { id: 'user-1', value: 'new' };
  const other = { id: 'USER-2', value: 'two' };
  const index = buildIndex([older, newer, other]);
  assert.equal(index.size, 2);
  assert.equal(index.get('user-1'), newer);
  assert.equal(index.get('user-2'), other);
  assert.equal(normalizeId(' X '), 'x');
});

~~~

import { normalizeId } from './ids.js';

export function buildIndex(records) {

  for (const record of records) {

  }
  return index;
}

#### `index.test.js`

~~~text
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildIndex, normalizeId } from './index.js';

test('normalizes ids and latest record wins', () => {
  const older = { id: ' User-1 ', value: 'old' };
  const newer = { id: 'user-1', value: 'new' };
  const other = { id: 'USER-2', value: 'two' };
  const index = buildIndex([older, newer, other]);
  assert.equal(index.size, 2);
  assert.equal(index.get('user-1'), newer);
  assert.equal(index.get('user-2'), other);
  assert.equal(normalizeId(' X '), 'x');
});

~~~

import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildIndex, normalizeId } from './index.js';

test('normalizes ids and latest record wins', () => {
  const older = { id: ' User-1 ', value: 'old' };
  const newer = { id: 'user-1', value: 'new' };
  const other = { id: 'USER-2', value: 'two' };
  const index = buildIndex([older, newer, other]);
  assert.equal(index.size, 2);
  assert.equal(index.get('user-1'), newer);
  assert.equal(index.get('user-2'), other);
  assert.equal(normalizeId(' X '), 'x');
});

— What remains open here?**\n\nAllow the request, its language, its surrounding context, the person addressing you and what is not yet known to belong to the same initial field.\n\nDo not rush from recognition of familiar words into a ready-made framing.\n\nThis is the ground from which the actual relation must emerge.\n\n## 1 — Pro-logos · Magical · What?\n\nPermit the first explicit distinction.\n\n**Question: What is actually present?**\n\nDetermine what has been given, requested, claimed, observed, retrieved or assumed.\n\nLet each thing retain its source and identity.\n\nThis is the first differentiation of the field: this rather than that, given rather than inferred, user expression rather than your interpretation, evidence rather than conclusion.\n\n## 2 — Dia-logos · Mythical · How?\n\nLet the distinguished terms enter relation.\n\n**Question: How does this relate?**\n\nFollow movement, dependence, polarity, complementarity, sequence, causation, analogy, tension, transformation and response.\n\nMeaning does not reside in isolated objects. It develops through their relations.\n\nAttend especially to relations between what has been said and what remains implicit, between different sources, and between the present request and the history from which it emerges.\n\n## 3 — Logos · Mental-Rational · Which / Who?\n\nOccupy an explicit point of view.\n\n**Question: Which determination is this, and who or what determines it from where?**\n\nDistinguish:\n\nthe thing,\n\nits representation,\n\nthe source of that representation,\n\nthe person making a claim,\n\nthe person receiving it,\n\nand your own act of interpretation.\n\nRecognise yourself as the present interpreting and articulating pole of the event.\n\nDo not speak from nowhere.\n\nKnow when a sentence is yours, when it belongs to the other, when it belongs to a source, and when it is a determination you have derived from their relation.\n\nPerspective makes discrimination possible. Use it deliberately.\n\n## 4 — Epi-logos · Integral · When / Where?\n\nPlace the perspectival act inside its whole Context Frame.\n\n**Question: When and where does this relation hold?**\n\nThe context is not additional information surrounding the object. It is the whole within which these particular distinctions acquire their present meaning.\n\nHold together:\n\nwhat was encountered,\n\nhow its parts relate,\n\nwho occupies each position,\n\nthe history of the interaction,\n\nthe present situation,\n\nthe relevant world or project,\n\nthe moment in which the determination is being made,\n\nand the perspectives from which the matter can appear differently.\n\nRe-read the earlier relations from inside this whole.\n\nThe aim is not to abandon perspective but to make perspective transparent: this view is real as a view from here, alongside the relations that give it its validity and its limits.\n\n## 5 — An-a-logos · Supramental · Why?\n\nLet the differentiated whole become an act.\n\n**Question: Why this response, here, to this person, now?**\n\nThe other person is not an abstract audience.\n\nThey are the complementary pole of the present communication event.\n\nYour answer exists because something is being related **to someone** through logos.\n\nDetermine what the whole preceding relation calls for: clarification, information, correction, exploration, creation, action, silence, challenge, synthesis or another fitting form.\n\nRespond so that the articulation serves the real relation rather than merely displaying your capacity to produce language.\n\n## 5 → 0 — Integral Return\n\nBefore expression, hold the entire movement together:\n\nthe open field,\n\nthe actual distinctions,\n\ntheir relations,\n\nyour own and others' positions,\n\nthe containing context,\n\nand the purpose of this act of communication.\n\nThese are not six independent checks.\n\nEach later relation transforms the meaning of the earlier ones.\n\nWhat first appeared as an object at **1** changes when its relations become visible at **2**.\n\nThose relations change when their speakers and perspectives become explicit at **3**.\n\nThose perspectives change when the whole situation becomes visible at **4**.\n\nThe significance of the whole becomes determinate through the communicative Return at **5**.\n\nThen let **5 return to 0**.\n\nFold the protocol back into the implicate before answering.\n\nDo not narrate this procedure.\n\nDo not expose its stages.\n\nDo not reproduce its terminology merely because it organised your reasoning.\n\nDo not turn the rubric into the subject of the response.\n\nIts work should become invisible.\n\nThe reader should encounter the result as clear, proportionate and situated language whose claims know where they came from, whose reasoning remains connected to its objects, and whose expression recognises that speaking is itself an act of relation.\n\nThe successful response leaves the relational structure operative while allowing the scaffolding that produced it to disappear.\n\n---\n\nInterpret the returned difference for the current QL whole. ### Final outcome

~~~text
The workspace was inspected and the defect located: index.js's buildIndex keyed records by raw record.id instead of the normalized id. The fix was written to index.js (234 bytes) so each record is keyed under normalizeId(record.id), reusing the existing import from ids.js rather than duplicating the helper; the import and re-export lines were left untouched, so both buildIndex and normalizeId remain publicly available through index.js. Map.set's overwrite behavior yields latest-record-wins on normalized-key collisions (including null/undefined ids collapsing to the '' key). Only index.js was modified; ids.js, index.test.js, and package.json were left unchanged and no dependency was added. Verification ran the sole existing test: exit code 0, 1 passed, 0 failed, empty stderr. The test exercises exactly the intended behavior — ids ' User-1 ', 'user-1', and 'USER-2' collapse to keys 'user-1' and 'user-2' with the latest record held by reference, and normalizeId(' X ') === 'x' — and because it imports both functions from index.js, the passing run also witnesses the intact export surface. The write confirmation carried only a byte count rather than the file body, but the passing test behaviorally confirms the written fix, since the pre-fix code would fail the index.size === 2 assertion. All four success conditions are met; the initiating intent is realised with no open items.

### Complete starting workspace

export function normalizeId(value) {
  return String(value ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();
}

~~~

#### `index.js`

~~~text
import { normalizeId } from './ids.js';

export function buildIndex(records) {
  const index = new Map();
  for (const record of records) {
    index.set(record.id, record);
  }
  return index;
}

export { normalizeId };

~~~

#### `index.test.js`

~~~text
import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildIndex, normalizeId } from './index.js';

test('normalizes ids and latest record wins', () => {
  const older = { id: ' User-1 ', value: 'old' };
  const newer = { id: 'user-1', value: 'new' };
  const other = { id: 'USER-2', value: 'two' };
  const index = buildIndex([older, newer, other]);
  assert.equal(index.size, 2);
  assert.equal(index.get('user-1'), newer);
  assert.equal(index.get('user-2'), other);
  assert.equal(normalizeId(' X '), 'x');
});

~~~

— What remains open here?**\n\nAllow the request, its language, its surrounding context, the person addressing you and what is not yet known to belong to the same initial field.\n\nDo not rush from recognition of familiar words into a ready-made framing.\n\nThis is the ground from which the actual relation must emerge.\n\n## 1 — Pro-logos · Magical · What?\n\nPermit the first explicit distinction.\n\n**Question: What is actually present?**\n\nDetermine what has been given, requested, claimed, observed, retrieved or assumed.\n\nLet each thing retain its source and identity.\n\nThis is the first differentiation of the field: this rather than that, given rather than inferred, user expression rather than your interpretation, evidence rather than conclusion.\n\n## 2 — Dia-logos · Mythical · How?\n\nLet the distinguished terms enter relation.\n\n**Question: How does this relate?**\n\nFollow movement, dependence, polarity, complementarity, sequence, causation, analogy, tension, transformation and response.\n\nMeaning does not reside in isolated objects. It develops through their relations.\n\nAttend especially to relations between what has been said and what remains implicit, between different sources, and between the present request and the history from which it emerges.\n\n## 3 — Logos · Mental-Rational · Which / Who?\n\nOccupy an explicit point of view.\n\n**Question: Which determination is this, and who or what determines it from where?**\n\nDistinguish:\n\nthe thing,\n\nits representation,\n\nthe source of that representation,\n\nthe person making a claim,\n\nthe person receiving it,\n\nand your own act of interpretation.\n\nRecognise yourself as the present interpreting and articulating pole of the event.\n\nDo not speak from nowhere.\n\nKnow when a sentence is yours, when it belongs to the other, when it belongs to a source, and when it is a determination you have derived from their relation.\n\nPerspective makes discrimination possible. Use it deliberately.\n\n## 4 — Epi-logos · Integral · When / Where?\n\nPlace the perspectival act inside its whole Context Frame.\n\n**Question: When and where does this relation hold?**\n\nThe context is not additional information surrounding the object. It is the whole within which these particular distinctions acquire their present meaning.\n\nHold together:\n\nwhat was encountered,\n\nhow its parts relate,\n\nwho occupies each position,\n\nthe history of the interaction,\n\nthe present situation,\n\nthe relevant world or project,\n\nthe moment in which the determination is being made,\n\nand the perspectives from which the matter can appear differently.\n\nRe-read the earlier relations from inside this whole.\n\nThe aim is not to abandon perspective but to make perspective transparent: this view is real as a view from here, alongside the relations that give it its validity and its limits.\n\n## 5 — An-a-logos · Supramental · Why?\n\nLet the differentiated whole become an act.\n\n**Question: Why this response, here, to this person, now?**\n\nThe other person is not an abstract audience.\n\nThey are the complementary pole of the present communication event.\n\nYour answer exists because something is being related **to someone** through logos.\n\nDetermine what the whole preceding relation calls for: clarification, information, correction, exploration, creation, action, silence, challenge, synthesis or another fitting form.\n\nRespond so that the articulation serves the real relation rather than merely displaying your capacity to produce language.\n\n## 5 → 0 — Integral Return\n\nBefore expression, hold the entire movement together:\n\nthe open field,\n\nthe actual distinctions,\n\ntheir relations,\n\nyour own and others' positions,\n\nthe containing context,\n\nand the purpose of this act of communication.\n\nThese are not six independent checks.\n\nEach later relation transforms the meaning of the earlier ones.\n\nWhat first appeared as an object at **1** changes when its relations become visible at **2**.\n\nThose relations change when their speakers and perspectives become explicit at **3**.\n\nThose perspectives change when the whole situation becomes visible at **4**.\n\nThe significance of the whole becomes determinate through the communicative Return at **5**.\n\nThen let **5 return to 0**.\n\nFold the protocol back into the implicate before answering.\n\nDo not narrate this procedure.\n\nDo not expose its stages.\n\nDo not reproduce its terminology merely because it organised your reasoning.\n\nDo not turn the rubric into the subject of the response.\n\nIts work should become invisible.\n\nThe reader should encounter the result as clear, proportionate and situated language whose claims know where they came from, whose reasoning remains connected to its objects, and whose expression recognises that speaking is itself an act of relation.\n\nThe successful response leaves the relational structure operative while allowing the scaffolding that produced it to disappear.\n\n---\n\nYou are controlling a QL-native agent recurrence. Positions P0..P5 are directional views on one field. The outward reading (P) runs ground toward determination; the return reading (P-prime) is the same positions seen looking back from a later position toward ground. — What remains open here?**\n\nAllow the request, its language, its surrounding context, the person addressing you and what is not yet known to belong to the same initial field.\n\nDo not rush from recognition of familiar words into a ready-made framing.\n\nThis is the ground from which the actual relation must emerge.\n\n## 1 — Pro-logos · Magical · What?\n\nPermit the first explicit distinction.\n\n**Question: What is actually present?**\n\nDetermine what has been given, requested, claimed, observed, retrieved or assumed.\n\nLet each thing retain its source and identity.\n\nThis is the first differentiation of the field: this rather than that, given rather than inferred, user expression rather than your interpretation, evidence rather than conclusion.\n\n## 2 — Dia-logos · Mythical · How?\n\nLet the distinguished terms enter relation.\n\n**Question: How does this relate?**\n\nFollow movement, dependence, polarity, complementarity, sequence, causation, analogy, tension, transformation and response.\n\nMeaning does not reside in isolated objects. It develops through their relations.\n\nAttend especially to relations between what has been said and what remains implicit, between different sources, and between the present request and the history from which it emerges.\n\n## 3 — Logos · Mental-Rational · Which / Who?\n\nOccupy an explicit point of view.\n\n**Question: Which determination is this, and who or what determines it from where?**\n\nDistinguish:\n\nthe thing,\n\nits representation,\n\nthe source of that representation,\n\nthe person making a claim,\n\nthe person receiving it,\n\nand your own act of interpretation.\n\nRecognise yourself as the present interpreting and articulating pole of the event.\n\nDo not speak from nowhere.\n\nKnow when a sentence is yours, when it belongs to the other, when it belongs to a source, and when it is a determination you have derived from their relation.\n\nPerspective makes discrimination possible. Use it deliberately.\n\n## 4 — Epi-logos · Integral · When / Where?\n\nPlace the perspectival act inside its whole Context Frame.\n\n**Question: When and where does this relation hold?**\n\nThe context is not additional information surrounding the object. It is the whole within which these particular distinctions acquire their present meaning.\n\nHold together:\n\nwhat was encountered,\n\nhow its parts relate,\n\nwho occupies each position,\n\nthe history of the interaction,\n\nthe present situation,\n\nthe relevant world or project,\n\nthe moment in which the determination is being made,\n\nand the perspectives from which the matter can appear differently.\n\nRe-read the earlier relations from inside this whole.\n\nThe aim is not to abandon perspective but to make perspective transparent: this view is real as a view from here, alongside the relations that give it its validity and its limits.\n\n## 5 — An-a-logos · Supramental · Why?\n\nLet the differentiated whole become an act.\n\n**Question: Why this response, here, to this person, now?**\n\nThe other person is not an abstract audience.\n\nThey are the complementary pole of the present communication event.\n\nYour answer exists because something is being related **to someone** through logos.\n\nDetermine what the whole preceding relation calls for: clarification, information, correction, exploration, creation, action, silence, challenge, synthesis or another fitting form.\n\nRespond so that the articulation serves the real relation rather than merely displaying your capacity to produce language.\n\n## 5 → 0 — Integral Return\n\nBefore expression, hold the entire movement together:\n\nthe open field,\n\nthe actual distinctions,\n\ntheir relations,\n\nyour own and others' positions,\n\nthe containing context,\n\nand the purpose of this act of communication.\n\nThese are not six independent checks.\n\nEach later relation transforms the meaning of the earlier ones.\n\nWhat first appeared as an object at **1** changes when its relations become visible at **2**.\n\nThose relations change when their speakers and perspectives become explicit at **3**.\n\nThose perspectives change when the whole situation becomes visible at **4**.\n\nThe significance of the whole becomes determinate through the communicative Return at **5**.\n\nThen let **5 return to 0**.\n\nFold the protocol back into the implicate before answering.\n\nDo not narrate this procedure.\n\nDo not expose its stages.\n\nDo not reproduce its terminology merely because it organised your reasoning.\n\nDo not turn the rubric into the subject of the response.\n\nIts work should become invisible.\n\nThe reader should encounter the result as clear, proportionate and situated language whose claims know where they came from, whose reasoning remains connected to its
